title: Option Injection via Unfiltered Flags
platform_conditions: POSIX sh and bash on Linux/macOS; '--' end-of-options convention follows the POSIX Utility Syntax Guidelines, which not every third-party utility implements
security_mechanism: Most POSIX utilities parse an operand that begins with '-' as an option, so an attacker who controls a filename or argument can turn data into flags: a file named '-n' or '--output' passed unguarded to cat, sort or cp changes the invoked behavior instead of being read. Without '--', there is no syntax boundary between the option region and operands, and utilities that do support '--' still differ on which options consume the next word. Glob expansion has the same shape: a pattern supplied by the user that matches nothing stays literal (nullglob off), and xargs without -0 splits its input on quotes and whitespace, letting a crafted filename inject entirely new arguments.

source_sink_clues.source: Untrusted filenames (uploads, archive members, directory listings of shared paths), user-chosen argument values in wrappers, and output of tools piped into xargs.
source_sink_clues.sink: Utility invocations where an input-derived value follows the command name with no '--' separator: cat/sort/head/cp/mv/kill, tar with input-derived flags, xargs without -0 or -d, git/curl wrapper scripts forwarding user arguments

tracking_guards: Check a literal '--' precedes every input-derived operand; check xargs uses -0 (with find -print0 / sort -z) or -d '\n'; check input-derived values are prefixed or validated to reject a leading '-' (case $arg in -*) reject); check glob results are iterated with quoted "$@" so each match is one operand.
not_candidate_when: The operand is validated against a grammar that cannot start with '-' (numeric IDs, absolute paths built server-side), '--' is already present before the operand and the target utility implements it, or xargs -0 pairs with NUL-delimited producers so injection through quoting is impossible.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
